_: Every divergence from the frozen spec, with the reason it exists. scripts/parity-check.mjs fails on a divergence that is not declared here AND on a declaration that no longer describes one, so this file cannot quietly become a list of things the check has stopped looking at. Keys beginning with _ are notes, not declarations. Reasons are the ones the code already carries in src/app/redesign-shell.css; this is where a reviewer reads them all at once.

_uncompared.src/app/redesign-hero.css: S2a's sheet. The only vendored spec is S1's shell.css and the S2 snapshot ships no CSS at all - its styles are inline in index.html - so there is nothing to compare this against yet. Comparing it to S1's shell reports nine divergences that are not divergences: that document is not about the hero. Freeze an S2 spec the way S1's was frozen and move this sheet into the comparison; until then this line is the record that it is NOT covered.

_spec: design/spec/S1-20260915T1938Z/shell.css, the <style> blocks of the frozen S1 snapshot the shell was transcribed from.
_clamp: The three below are one departure in three rules: the design's one-screen clamp, overridden while the views still hold pre-redesign content. Shipping it clipped the footer by 30 to 93px at ordinary laptop sizes with three links unreachable. It returns with the content designed for it, S2 to S5, enforced per slice by scripts/fit-check.mjs.
_form: Each entry names WHY it differs and WHAT we ship. The body matters: declared by selector alone, a second, different change to an already-declared rule inherits the old label - measured, an added outline on .badge .dot passed. Regenerate the bodies with PARITY_PRINT=1 node scripts/parity-check.mjs <spec> <shipped...> and keep the why.

.badge[data-state=DEGRADED],.badge[data-.why: Same: real states the preview has no swatch for.

.badge[data-state=PREPARING],.badge[data.why: The preview's badge knows LIVE and SYNCING. Our phase machine says more, and those words were already carrying meaning on the page before the redesign.

.brand .home .brand-mark.why: Our mark is an SVG component where the preview's is a canvas, so the preview's canvas rules do not apply to it.

.brand .home:focus-visible.why: The same correction one specificity level up: this rule sets the whole outline shorthand, so correcting the general rule left the masthead link at 2.53:1 until this moved with it.

.ftr nav a,.hdr-right nav a.why: WCAG 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1 and the preview's --muted is 4.41:1 on --page. --label is 4.96:1, the next token up rather than a new colour.

.stage.why: The one-screen clamp overridden: height:auto with min-height, and container-type:inline-size, because size containment needs a definite height in both axes and 1cqw goes with it.
.stage.shipped: container-type:inline-size; height:auto; min-height:100dvh; overflow:visible || container:stage / size; height:100dvh; overflow:auto; --u:clamp(10.5px,calc(1cqw * var(--cards-scale)),14px)

.view.legacy-measure > *.why: Transitional, one view at a time as S2 to S5 land: the moved pre-redesign content keeps the 760px measure it was written for, inside a full-width view. src/app/legacyMeasure.test.ts fails in both directions on it and ui-smoke measures the width itself.

.views.why: Our own <main> landmark around the four sections. The preview puts them straight into .comp; a landmark is an accessibility requirement a static preview does not have to meet.
.views.shipped: display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:calc(2.6*var(--u)); flex:1; width:100%; min-width:0

:focus-visible.why: RE-SCOPED TO OUTRANK globals.css, SAME DECLARATIONS (#575). We ship this as `html :focus-visible`, declared separately with the body. Under the spec's own key we now ship nothing, which is the dropped half of one re-scoping rather than a rule we lost. The previous declaration here carried the body from before the move and would have gone on describing a rule that no longer exists at this selector.

@media (max-width:32rem) | .strip.why: WCAG 2.5.5 target size at the phone breakpoint: 32px to 44px.

@media (min-width:56rem) | .comp.why: The same override: the spec pins .comp to 100dvh here.

@media (min-width:56rem) | .stage.why: The same override at the desktop breakpoint, where the spec sets overflow:hidden.

.blindfold.why: THE MASCOT'S INNER DOM IS THE `page-mascot` PACKAGE'S, NOT OURS. The design draws the fox from its own markup - .m-body, .m-head, .m-head-img, .m-tails, .blindfold inside .mascot-frame - and we render <Mascot/> from the package instead, which ships its own structure and its own styling. Transcribing these would be a second, competing description of a DOM we do not author; the first time the package changed its internals ours would be dead CSS pointing at elements that no longer exist. The visual result is checked where it can be: scripts/mascot-check.mjs measures the rendered fox in the page rather than the rules behind it.

.comp > .view.hero.why: RE-SCOPED TO OUTRANK globals.css, SAME DECLARATIONS (#575). The legacy sheet styles the same element at the same specificity, so the design's own selector loses on source order alone. One ancestor is added - `html` for element rules, `.stage` for page furniture - which raises specificity without changing what is painted. The spec's key and ours therefore differ while the CSS does not, and the checker reports that as one dropped rule plus one added rule: the same divergence twice.

.tip.why: A GAP, NOT A DECISION, and it is declared here only so the gate can measure the other two hundred rules rather than stopping on this one. The design's drips chart carries a hover tooltip - the rule at shell.css:287, the element at index.html:637 inside the Analytics chart - and we ship neither. Filed as #594 against the sheet owner rather than declared away quietly. When the tooltip ships, this entry stops describing a divergence and the checker demands its removal, which is the property that stops this line becoming permanent.
